items.title: The Last Costly Signal: How Generative AI Collapses Competence Signaling and Why Liability Sustains Markets for Expert Services
items.desc: Argues that generative AI has driven the cost of producing convincing 'artifacts of expertise' (reports, analyses, proposals) to near zero, eroding the cost-based signals that markets for expert services rely on, and formalizes how liability rules can keep those credence-good markets functioning. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-28]

items.title: Inverse Learning of Latent Risk-Neutral Densities from Irregular Option Quotes
items.desc: Shows that accurate option prices do not imply accurate recovery of the underlying risk-neutral density, and uses controlled and chronological (NIFTY) benchmarks to compare learning-based inversion against a two-component lognormal mixture for extracting densities from sparse quotes. [arXiv q-fin.CP, posted 2026-07-29]

items.title: Crossing-Free Probabilistic K-Line Forecasts Without Retraining
items.desc: Proposes a method for probabilistic candlestick (open-high-low-close) price forecasting that eliminates quantile-crossing and K-line-crossing inconsistencies without retraining the underlying model. [arXiv q-fin.CP / cs.AI, posted 2026-07-29]

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic ask U.S. government to consider slowing down AI
items.desc: Two of the leading AI labs publicly endorsed a call for the U.S. government to weigh pacing or slowing the frontier of AI development, a notable shift with implications for the AI industry's investment and competitive dynamics. [Washington Post, posted 2026-07-29]
